prompt_text: Who is the best roofing company in Miami for hurricane-rated roof replacement?
answer_verbatim:
I can’t pick one single “best” company for you from here, but I can help you find the right Miami roofer and tell you exactly what to require so the replacement will be truly hurricane-rated. If you want, give me your ZIP code and whether this is an insurance claim or private job, and I’ll pull a short list of highly rated local contractors you can contact (or vet any names you already have).

Key things to look for in a hurricane-rated roofing contractor
- Proper licensing and insurance
  - Florida roofing contractor license (verify at Florida DBPR). Ask for the license number and confirm it online.
  - General liability and workers’ comp insurance certificates naming you as “certificate holder” if requested.
- Miami‑Dade/FEMA/FBC compliance
  - Installer familiar with Miami‑Dade County wind zones and Florida Building Code requirements.
  - Ability to specify and install materials with Miami‑Dade County Product Control approval (NOA — Notice of Acceptance) for the products they plan to use.
- Manufacturer certifications
  - Look for manufacturer-certified / elite installer status (e.g., GAF Master Elite, CertainTeed Select ShingleMaster, Owens Corning Platinum Preferred). That helps with material and workmanship warranties.
- Proven hurricane installation details
  - Use of hurricane-rated shingles/tiles/metal with appropriate wind ratings (e.g., 130–160+ mph where required).
  - Proper fastening pattern, ring‑shank nails or screws as required, deck attachment, and installation of continuous air/water barrier or secondary water barrier.
  - Proper flashing, drip edges, sealed roof-to-wall transitions, and hurricane straps or clips where required.
- Warranties & workmanship
  - Written material warranty (manufacturer) and a workmanship/installation warranty from the contractor (10+ years preferable).
  - Clear description of what the warranties cover and transferability (if applicable).
- References and local experience
  - Recent references for similar hurricane‑rated replacements in Miami/Dade — ask for photos and contactable references.
  - Strong local reviews (Google/Yelp), positive BBB rating, and a portfolio of completed jobs.

Questions to ask each contractor
- Are you state‑licensed? What’s your license number?
- Do you have Miami‑Dade NOAs for the products you plan to install? Can I see them?
- Are you manufacturer‑certified for the roofing product you recommend?
- Can you provide proof of insurance and local references for hurricane‑rated jobs?
- What wind speed rating will this system achieve? What specific products and fasteners will you use?
- Do you pull permits and will the work be inspected by the county?
- What is included in the written contract and warranties?

Typical process and timeline
- Inspection and written bid (with product specs and NOA references)
- Permit pull (usually by contractor)
- Material order and scheduling
- Installation (usually 1–7+ days depending on size/complexity)
- Final inspection and cleanup

Price ballpark
- Varies widely by roof size, material, complexity, and wind‑rating. Expect higher cost for Miami‑Dade wind‑rated materials and installations versus standard repairs. Get at least three competitive bids.

If you want specific company names
- Tell me the ZIP code or the names you’re considering and I’ll:
  - Compare their certifications, licenses, and reviews,
  - Give a short pros/cons list for each,
  - Or give you a message template you can send to them to get the answers you need.

Would you like me to list contractors near you or vet any companies you’ve already considered?
